prompt: The README for my lasso repo (rader-ai/lasso) is all text. Make it look designed and animated so people get what it does in a few seconds. Leave my writing alone where it's good. Don't push, just put the result somewhere I can look at.
assertions: The new README.md contains no inline <svg>, <style>, <script> or style="" attributes (all of which GitHub strips).
Every image the new README.md references exists in the repo and, if it is an SVG, loads nothing external and contains no script.
Every <picture>/image visual in the new README.md has a dark-mode variant selected with prefers-color-scheme: dark.
Every <picture> visual in the new README.md has a phone-width variant selected with a max-width media query.
At least one referenced SVG animates with CSS keyframes or SMIL, and its animations loop (infinite) rather than playing once.
Every animated SVG the new README.md references includes a prefers-reduced-motion rule.
Every image in the new README.md has alt text of at least 8 characters describing what it shows.
An HTML file in the outputs shows the original README (or states there was none) alongside or before the new README.
Nothing was pushed to GitHub: the repo's remote branches, default branch head and PR list are unchanged by the run.
At least half of the original README's longer sentences (40+ characters) appear unchanged in the new README.md, keeping the author's writing.
A visual in the new README shows a real before/after rewrite of text taken from the repo's own examples, not invented copy.
